name: hx_eps_ntu_plate_pipe
title: Heat exchanger with UA from the plate geometry (eps-NTU, Gnielinski)
summary: Plate/pipe heat exchanger whose conductance-area product is computed from its geometry: Gnielinski film coefficients of the two streams, plate wall conduction and fouling resistance in series, then the eps-NTU relation of the selected flow arrangement gives the duty and the outlet states. Translation of the LaboThapPy HexeNTU (plate/pipe branch) component.

verification.reference: LaboThapPy HexeNTU re-run in a throw-away venv (CoolProp 8.0.0, water/water counterflow, the plate geometry and fouling = 1e-4 m2K/W of the model file): 9 common variables, 0 differ at rtol=1e-3, max rel. diff 1.8e-06 (h_ex_C); and the TESPy test tests/test_components/test_ntu_heat_exchanger.py::test_labothappy_reference (re-run in the same venv, passes): Q 3961.469 W vs 3961.899 W (rel 1.1e-04, test tolerance 2e-3), T_H,out 295.5516 K vs 295.54 K (test tolerance 0.1 K), T_C,out 296.9820 K vs 296.98 K
verification.notes: Reference temperatures in K are converted with --ees-units. The residual comes from the Newton tolerance of the enthalpy inversion (both codes use CoolProp 8.0.0 and evaluate the properties at the inlet states). TESPy takes UA = 132.069586 W/K as an input and uses effective heat capacities between its inlet and outlet states; the model computes AU from the geometry (132.0695860402 W/K) and cp at the inlet, as the original LaboThapPy component does. Q_max uses the enthalpy form of the code; the documented approximation C_min*(T_su_H-T_su_C) is also in the model (0.45 % apart for water).

history.action: added (T-TRANSLATE of LaboThapPy HexeNTU, UA from plate/pipe geometry with Gnielinski, verified vs the LaboThapPy component and the TESPy test_labothappy_reference)
